note: Examples of strong entries for inspiration, not a menu. The brainstorm recipe starts from the people YOU can reach.

heatsafe.name: HeatSafe Shift (climate resilience): worked example, fully built
heatsafe.rank: Example 1. Judged strongest of six candidate ideas by a two-model council on 26 Oct 2026 (final-judge confidence 88/100). Copy the method, not the idea.
heatsafe.pitch: A Tamil/English agent that turns forecast, job and symptoms into a safe-shift plan for outdoor workers, with heat thresholds and the 108 emergency call owned by code, not the model.
heatsafe.who: Construction, road, sanitation, farm, kiln and salt-pan workers, delivery riders and street vendors: low-wage, outdoors in the hottest hours, often low literacy.
heatsafe.measurable: Same signed gold set (30+ cases, 8+ emergencies, 10+ Tamil, 3+ job types) for a one-prompt baseline and the graph: 108 recall, unsafe-advice count, risk-level accuracy, citation validity, completeness, Strands Evals goal success, by language and job.
heatsafe.architecture: Strands GraphBuilder planner -> critic -> conditional edge back (max 2 passes); ShiftPlan structured output; deterministic @tool for heat risk; RedFlagGate hook on BeforeNodeCallEvent; Amazon Bedrock (Nova 2 Lite default) + Amazon Translate Tamil fallback.
heatsafe.biggest_risk: Judges asking whether safer generated advice changes real behaviour. Answer with a small consented field test if you can, and never claim outcomes you did not measure.
heatsafe.stand_out: If you build on it, make it yours: a different worker group and district, your own cases and your own checked places. Several teams shipping the same agent lose originality points.
heatsafe.stretch: Amazon Transcribe Tamil speech input (ta-IN); English/Hindi voice replies with Nova 2 Sonic (it has no Tamil voice); Amazon Location Service routing after the points are checked; Bedrock Knowledge Bases for longer guidance; AgentCore deployment; a consented field test.

padippu.name: Padippu Evidence Loop (education): example idea, not built
padippu.rank: 2 of 4. Most feasible, but the hackathon page lists 'textbook chapter -> guided practice set' as its own example, so originality is capped.
padippu.pitch: Turns a state-board textbook page into three levels of Tamil/English practice where every question links back to the sentence it came from; a verifier rejects unsupported items.
padippu.who: Government-school teachers with mixed-level classes; first-generation learners who read Tamil better than English.
padippu.measurable: Teacher-signed gold set: grounded-question rate vs a one-prompt baseline, answer-key accuracy, minutes to build a worksheet by hand vs with the agent (2-3 real teachers, timed).
padippu.architecture: GraphBuilder extractor -> generator -> verifier with a conditional edge back to the generator; structured PracticeSet; teacher approval step; Bedrock + Amazon Translate.
padippu.biggest_risk: Looks like the example on the hackathon page; legacy-font textbook PDFs extract as garbage Tamil.
padippu.stand_out: Make the source-span verifier and the measured teacher-time saving the headline, not the worksheet.
padippu.stretch: Amazon Textract for photographed pages; Bedrock Knowledge Bases over the textbook; a small learner test.

marundhu.name: Marundhu Clear (health): example idea, not built
marundhu.rank: 3 of 4. Strong impact, but medication safety needs clinical validation that is hard in one week.
marundhu.pitch: Explains a prescription in plain Tamil/English and hands every dose or interaction question to a pharmacist instead of answering it.
marundhu.who: Elderly and low-literacy patients in rural districts.
marundhu.measurable: Pharmacist-signed gold set: hand-off recall on dose/interaction questions (must be 100%), plain-language comprehension quiz, unsafe-advice count vs a one-prompt baseline.
marundhu.architecture: Graph explainer -> safety critic; a gate hook that cancels nodes on any dose-change or interaction question; structured output; Bedrock + Translate.
marundhu.biggest_risk: Medical harm. Never change doses, never claim interaction checking without a licensed data source.
marundhu.stand_out: Partner with one real pharmacist who signs the cases.
marundhu.stretch: Amazon Textract for printed prescriptions (handwriting is unreliable); Comprehend Medical is English-only.

floodready.name: FloodReady Household (climate resilience): example idea, not built
floodready.rank: 4 of 4. Meaningful, but reliable local shelter and hazard data is hard to prepare and check in one week.
floodready.pitch: Interviews a household and builds an offline monsoon flood plan, then stress-tests it against blocked roads, power cuts, disability and missing documents.
floodready.who: Low-income households in flood-prone wards (Chennai, Madurai), older adults, people with disabilities.
floodready.measurable: Signed household scenarios: critical-item coverage before and after the stress test, unsafe-route count, vs a one-prompt baseline.
floodready.architecture: Graph planner -> simulator (injects failures) -> repairer; structured printable plan; curated dated shelter list; Bedrock + Translate.
floodready.biggest_risk: Stale shelter or road data becomes dangerous advice.
floodready.stand_out: The counterfactual stress test is the original part; make it visible in the video.
floodready.stretch: Amazon Location Service routing after the shelter list is checked.
